newsitem.title: UK: Oil rigs in northwest Europe to rise to 61 in 97.
newsitem.headline: Oil rigs in northwest Europe to rise to 61 in 97.

text.p: Oil rigs exploring and appraising finds in Northwest Europe are forecast to rise by five to 61 rigs this year, said analysts Wood Mackenzie.
Norway is expected to start 35 wells this year compared to 25 in 1996 but Holland is due to start 22 compared to 28 last year, Wood Mackenzie said a report.
Denmark is forecast to start four wells compared to three in 1996.

In Norway companies are tending to plan for future drilling using conservative oil prices assumptions and as a result drilling programmes should be more robust and able to withstand a downturn in the oil price. Growth in drilling activity should be sustainable, the report said.
In 1996, just 25 new wells were started because there was a shortage of suitable rigs. Some 13 wells were deferred until this year.
Oil companies have proposed 40 exploration and appraisal wells this year but due to the shortage is seems unlikely that this level of activity will be achievable.
The report forecast 35 wells will actually be started this year which will boost the total amount of rig time, measured in rig years, to 6.6 rig years from 5.1.
Development drilling in Norway will also rise sharply this year to 13.9 rig years from 9.2 rig years last year, the report said.

In the Netherlands, the forecast fall this year to 22 from 28 exploration and appraisal wells is due to the small size of gas fields found in the Dutch sector of the North Sea. It is rarely necessary, nor economically prudent, to further appraise the relatively small gas structures which were discovered, the report said.

In Denmark the four exploration and appraisal wells are due to start this year, all drilled by one rig. But the rig's arrival from Argentina has been delayed which may curtail the drilling programme because it is due to move to the Norwegian sector of the North Sea in August to help develop Saga Petroleum's Varg field.Saga Petroleum
